title: How Codex Works — Dominik Kundel, OpenAI
talk_summary: Dominik Kundel walks through the internals of the open-source Codex harness: how context is assembled and capped, how tools are deferred and discovered, how sub-agents/background terminals/computer-use/file-editing work, how sandbox auto-review reduces approval fatigue, and how WebSocket transport plus server-side compaction keep long runs fast and cheap.

takeaways.what_they_do: Tools (especially MCP-provided ones) are marked deferred so they are not in the context window; the model discovers them via a tool-search tool only when needed.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we're marking some of these tools as deferred, and that means that they're not added directly to the context window, but instead are available through tool search later on

takeaways.technique: Cap skills list at 2% of context
takeaways.what_they_do: The available-skills list is capped at 2% of the max context window; when it exceeds that, descriptions are progressively shortened.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we actually cap the available skills list at 2% of your context total like maximum context window

takeaways.what_they_do: When an agent tries to escalate out of the sandbox, a separate read-only subagent (cannot spawn subagents) judges the action using user authorization, risk taxonomy, transcript and tool calls, auto-approving low-risk actions and blocking exfiltration.
takeaways.evidence_quote: this subagent runs entirely separate and can't spin up other subagents and has read permissions only

takeaways.what_they_do: The main agent gets a spawn_agent tool plus send_input, wait, and shutdown, so it can delegate and keep working; the same pattern powers background terminals via stdin.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we give the agent a spawn agent tool, which then allows the agent to create new new agent instances, and then use a send input tool

takeaways.what_they_do: Long transcripts are automatically compacted into a new context containing a compaction item, trained-for so performance holds, triggered manually or automatically.
takeaways.evidence_quote: automatically trigger compaction on the server side in a way that the model got trained with so that the performance stays the same

takeaways.technique: Goal loop with continuation prompt + explicit done tool
takeaways.what_they_do: For /goal, the harness injects a continuation prompt containing the objective each turn until the model calls an update_goal tool declaring completion; goals must be concrete and verifiable.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the harness will inject this continuation prompt ... until the model itself calls an update plan update goal tool
